Class SecretResolver

java.lang.Object
io.baleia.trino.catalogstore.SecretResolver
public class SecretResolver extends Object
Replaces @baleia-secret[<origin>:<key>] with the actual value. Three origin schemes are supported:
  • @baleia-secret[<catalog>:<key>] — another row in the database (existing)
  • @baleia-secret[file:<name>] — a file under baleia.secret-file-base-dir (new)
  • @baleia-secret[env:<VAR>] — an environment variable (new)

The CREATE CATALOG text — which Trino logs and exposes in the Web UI — never contains real credentials.

Why not ${baleia-secret:...}? The Trino CLI (and several other tools in the ecosystem — bash, picocli, Spring) interpret ${...} as a variable expansion before the SQL reaches our createCatalogProperties. The Trino server routes CREATE CATALOG properties straight through, but any client that does its own ${...} parsing will eat our placeholder. Using @baleia-secret[...] sidesteps every standard expansion syntax.

The substitution is total and verified: after resolution, the resolver confirms no output value still looks like a baleia-secret placeholder. This catches:

  • Unresolved placeholders that shape-match @baleia-secret[...] literally (e.g. the catalog segment is uppercase and the regex never matched).
  • A referenced secret whose stored value is itself a @baleia-secret[...] reference, i.e. a (deliberate or accidental) circular reference.
Both cases throw IllegalStateException, which BaleiaCatalogStore either fails the catalog load (boot path) or surfaces back to the user (DDL path) with.

  • Method Details

    • resolve

      public Map<String,String> resolve(Map<String,String> properties)
      Resolves all placeholders in the given properties map.

      Each value is checked against the @baleia-secret[...] pattern. Non-placeholder values pass through unchanged. The first group of the match determines the origin scheme:

      • file: — reads from a file under baleia.secret-file-base-dir
      • env: — reads from a process environment variable
      • anything else — treated as a catalog name, resolved via Database

      After resolution, every output value is verified to not itself be a placeholder, catching circular references and malformed inputs.

      Parameters:
      properties - the raw properties from the database or DDL
      Returns:
      a new map with all placeholders resolved
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if a placeholder cannot be resolved, a circular reference is detected, or a malformed placeholder is found
